verses.text: The lot for the tribe of the children of Judah according to their families was to the border of Edom, even to the wilderness of Zin southward, at the uttermost part of the south.
Their south border was from the uttermost part of the Salt Sea, from the bay that looks southward;
and it went out southward of the ascent of Akrabbim, and passed along to Zin, and went up by the south of Kadesh Barnea, and passed along by Hezron, went up to Addar, and turned towards Karka;
and it passed along to Azmon, went out at the brook of Egypt; and the border ended at the sea. This shall be your south border.
The east border was the Salt Sea, even to the end of the Jordan. The border of the north quarter was from the bay of the sea at the end of the Jordan.
The border went up to Beth Hoglah, and passed along by the north of Beth Arabah; and the border went up to the stone of Bohan the son of Reuben.

The border went up to Debir from the valley of Achor, and so northward, looking toward Gilgal, that faces the ascent of Adummim, which is on the south side of the river. The border passed along to the waters of En Shemesh, and ended at En Rogel.

The border went up by the valley of the son of Hinnom to the side of the Jebusite (also called Jerusalem) southward; and the border went up to the top of the mountain that lies before the valley of Hinnom westward, which is at the farthest part of the valley of Rephaim northward.
The border extended from the top of the mountain to the spring of the waters of Nephtoah, and went out to the cities of Mount Ephron; and the border extended to Baalah (also called Kiriath Jearim);

and the border turned about from Baalah westward to Mount Seir, and passed along to the side of Mount Jearim (also called Chesalon) on the north, and went down to Beth Shemesh, and passed along by Timnah;

and the border went out to the side of Ekron northward; and the border extended to Shikkeron, and passed along to Mount Baalah, and went out at Jabneel; and the goings out of the border were at the sea.
The west border was to the shore of the great sea. This is the border of the children of Judah according to their families.
He gave to Caleb the son of Jephunneh a portion among the children of Judah, according to the commandment of Yahweh to Joshua, even Kiriath Arba, named after the father of Anak (also called Hebron).
Caleb drove out the three sons of Anak: Sheshai, and Ahiman, and Talmai, the children of Anak.
He went up against the inhabitants of Debir: now the name of Debir before was Kiriath Sepher.
Caleb said, “He who strikes Kiriath Sepher, and takes it, to him I will give Achsah my daughter as wife.”
Othniel the son of Kenaz, the brother of Caleb, took it: and he gave him Achsah his daughter as wife.
When she came, she had him ask her father for a field. She got off of her donkey, and Caleb said, “What do you want?”
She said, “Give me a blessing. Because you have set me in the land of the South, give me also springs of water.” So he gave her the upper springs and the lower springs.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Judah according to their families.
The farthest cities of the tribe of the children of Judah toward the border of Edom in the South were Kabzeel, Eder, Jagur,
Kinah, Dimonah, Adadah,
Kedesh, Hazor, Ithnan,
Ziph, Telem, Bealoth,
Hazor Hadattah, Kerioth Hezron (also called Hazor),
Amam, Shema, Moladah,
Hazar Gaddah, Heshmon, Beth Pelet,
Hazar Shual, Beersheba, Biziothiah,
Baalah, Iim, Ezem,
Eltolad, Chesil, Hormah,
Ziklag, Madmannah, Sansannah,
Lebaoth, Shilhim, Ain, and Rimmon. All the cities are twenty-nine, with their villages.
In the lowland, Eshtaol, Zorah, Ashnah,
Zanoah, En Gannim, Tappuah, Enam,
Jarmuth, Adullam, Socoh, Azekah,
Shaaraim, Adithaim and Gederah (or Gederothaim); fourteen cities with their villages.
Zenan, Hadashah, Migdal Gad,
Dilean, Mizpah, Joktheel,
Lachish, Bozkath, Eglon,
Cabbon, Lahmam, Chitlish,
Gederoth, Beth Dagon, Naamah, and Makkedah; sixteen cities with their villages.
Libnah, Ether, Ashan,
Iphtah, Ashnah, Nezib,
Keilah, Achzib, and Mareshah; nine cities with their villages.
Ekron, with its towns and its villages;
from Ekron even to the sea, all that were by the side of Ashdod, with their villages.
Ashdod, its towns and its villages; Gaza, its towns and its villages; to the brook of Egypt, and the great sea with its coastline.
In the hill country, Shamir, Jattir, Socoh,
Dannah, Kiriath Sannah (which is Debir),
Anab, Eshtemoh, Anim,
Goshen, Holon, and Giloh; eleven cities with their villages.
Arab, Dumah, Eshan,
Janim, Beth Tappuah, Aphekah,
Humtah, Kiriath Arba (also called Hebron), and Zior; nine cities with their villages.
Maon, Carmel, Ziph, Jutah,
Jezreel, Jokdeam, Zanoah,
Kain, Gibeah, and Timnah; ten cities with their villages.
Halhul, Beth Zur, Gedor,
Maarath, Beth Anoth, and Eltekon; six cities with their villages.
Kiriath Baal (also called Kiriath Jearim), and Rabbah; two cities with their villages.
In the wilderness, Beth Arabah, Middin, Secacah,
Nibshan, the City of Salt, and En Gedi; six cities with their villages.
As for the Jebusites, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the children of Judah couldn’t drive them out; but the Jebusites live with the children of Judah at Jerusalem to this day.

footnotes.content: The Lord parcels out the land according to His promise, and Judah's portion stretches from Edom's border to the wilderness. See how the hand of the Lord still moves through lots? That's how He brings order—not chaos, but careful, deliberate boundaries that say to each tribe: *This* is your inheritance, *this* is where you belong.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Salt Sea marks Judah's eastern edge—that salt lake, always salty, never fresh. The Lord knew what land He was giving His people, even the hard parts. He doesn't give what's easy on its surface; He gives what's *true*, and from truth comes blessing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The ascent of Akrabbim, Zin, Kadesh Barnea—these names carry memory. Kadesh is where Israel failed in faith forty years before. Now Judah is walking toward that history, but the Lord is leading them through it, not away from it, to show that His mercy follows us even into the places we once stumbled.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The brook of Egypt marks the southern boundary—that same river that saw Moses lead Israel to freedom. Now Judah's inheritance reaches back to the edge of that memory. The Lord is saying: *Remember where I brought you from. This is where I bring you to.*
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Salt Sea, the Jordan's end—Judah is bounded by living water that once became a wall, and salt water that remembers judgment. What boundaries the Lord sets for us are always boundaries of grace, even when they feel like limits.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The stone of Bohan the son of Reuben—a marker named for a man, a sign that the tribes remember each other even as they settle in their own lands. The Lord's people don't live as islands; they're bound by shared history and shared memory.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Debir, Gilgal, Adummim—this border winds northward through places thick with God's story. Gilgal was where Israel first camped in the promised land. Now Judah's boundary touches it—a reminder that we inherit not empty real estate, but a land saturated with the Lord's faithfulness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The valley of Hinnom, the Jebusites, Jerusalem itself—the Lord gives Judah this territory, but the Jebusites still hold the city. It's not a defeat; it's a test of faith. Promises given aren't always promises kept in an instant. They're promises *being* kept.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Baalah, called Kiriath Jearim—this city will later hold the ark of the covenant. The Lord is mapping out Judah's inheritance with that future in His view already. He sees the whole story; we see the piece in our hands.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The border turns, winds, and passes through named places. How good that the Lord knows even these small places by name. He doesn't wave His hand vaguely; He marks the land, names it, and says: *You belong here. I know this corner of earth you're walking.*
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The border extends to the sea—Judah's possession reaches westward to the great water. It's a generous inheritance, and the Lord is showing Judah: *This is what I promised your father Abraham. This is real. This is yours.*
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The west border is the shore of the great sea—Judah's land is bounded, measured, and real. The Lord doesn't speak in vague promises; He speaks in geography, in rivers, in coastlines. He says: *Here. This is where I have placed you.*
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Caleb receives Hebron—and the Lord Himself commanded this gift, remembering Caleb's faith when all others doubted. Forty years of patience were rewarded. The Lord's memory is long, and His reward never expires. Caleb got his inheritance not by younger strength, but by older faith.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Caleb drove out the sons of Anak—giants who once made Israel's spies tremble. Now an old man chases them down. Don't let fear rob you of your inheritance; the Lord gives strength not to youth alone, but to those who trust Him long.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Debir—City of the Book—was a fortress of pagan worship. Caleb sets his sights on it. To truly inherit God's land, we must be willing to challenge what stands against Him, not with harsh judgment, but with faithfulness and courage.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Caleb stakes his own daughter as the prize—a beautiful picture of how the Lord rewards faithfulness with blessing. Achsah isn't a bargaining chip here; she's the fruit of her father's faith, offered to a man brave enough to match that courage.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Othniel the son of Kenaz answered the call—a younger man stepping up, and the Lord saw it. Out of this moment comes Othniel, who will later judge Israel and rescue them. Our faithfulness now plants the seeds of the Lord's future work in ways we may never fully know.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Achsah gets off her donkey and asks—a picture of a woman wise enough to seek provision early in her marriage. She's learned from her father to claim what the Lord promises, not to shrink back. Notice she doesn't ask timidly; she asks boldly, and her father hears her.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Springs of water in the dry south—Achsah doesn't ask for gold or war captives; she asks for what nourishes life. And Caleb gives her both upper and lower springs, full measure. The Lord loves when His people ask for life-giving gifts and aren't ashamed to receive them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The inheritance is summarized—families within Judah all receive their portions. This is how the Lord builds His people: not as a mass, but as families, each one known, each one blessed according to the pattern He set before time began.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Kabzeel, Eder, Jagur—cities in the far south of Judah. The Lord's land stretches to every corner, and He names them all. Not a city so remote or small that the Lord forgets it. His care reaches to the margins.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A long list of southern cities—Beersheba among them, where Abraham once dwelled. The Lord is giving Judah not just a land, but a history, woven through the very places they will settle. Every city carries a story, and together they tell of God's faithfulness from age to age.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: In the lowland—Eshtaol, Zorah, Ashnah. These lowland cities will one day harbor Samson, the judge. The Lord places His people and already knows what trials and triumphs are coming. He settles us right where we're needed.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: En Gannim, Tappuah—more lowland cities, more of Judah's inheritance spread out. The Lord isn't stingy with the land He gives His people; He gives generously, and generously we should hold it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Adullam is listed—this fortress will one day shelter David when he fled from Saul. Even now, the Lord places the cities where His future servants will need refuge. Providential placement centuries before the need arises.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Fourteen lowland cities, each real, each possessed. The Lord doesn't promise dream-land; He promises real places where real people live real lives of faith. And that's enough—more than enough.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Lachish among these cities—one day it will be a great fortress city, a key to Judah's defense. The Lord places His people for a purpose we often don't yet see. We settle, we build, we live—and find that we were placed exactly where we were meant to be.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Libnah, Ether, Ashan—more cities of the lowland. Each name is precious to the Lord; each place is part of His gift to His people. We live in a God who cares about geography, about borders, about the actual land where actual people live.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Keilah is here—a place David will later help defend. And Achzib, Mareshah—nine cities, each with their own history and future. The Lord gives land and people; what we do with it becomes our offering back to Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ekron was a Philistine stronghold—and now it's part of Judah's inheritance, listed as theirs. This isn't yet full possession, but it's the Lord's promise written down. What belongs to Him will one day be fully, finally possessed.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: From Ekron to the sea—Judah's western edge. The Lord's gift stretches far. To the Philistines, these coasts are contested ground; to Judah, they are inheritance. Perspective changes everything.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ashdod and Gaza—famous Philistine cities—are listed as Judah's inheritance. Again, not yet fully possessed, but promised. The Lord speaks of these cities as His gift before the conquest is complete, teaching Judah to *see* what He sees: the end from the beginning.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: In the hill country—Shamir, Jattir, Socoh. The Lord's land for Judah spans lowlands and highlands, coast and interior. His gifts are full and varied, designed to strengthen His people in every terrain.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Debir, called also Kiriath Sannah—the same city Caleb took by faith. Now it's listed as part of Judah's inheritance in the highlands. The Lord rewards faithfulness by making what we overcome part of our lasting blessing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Anab, Eshtemoh, Anim, Goshen, Holon, Giloh—eleven highland cities. The Lord scatters His people across varied terrain so that they learn to trust Him in every climate, every elevation, every circumstance.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hebron appears again in this highland list—Kiriath Arba, the city Caleb received. The Lord makes certain places belong to certain people because He knows what they need and what they will do with it. Caleb gets Hebron; he'll be faithful there.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Maon, Carmel, Ziph, Jutah—more highland cities. Ziph will later shelter David in caves when he's fleeing. The Lord places the wilderness cities where they'll be needed for the refuge of His faithful, even centuries ahead.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Halhul, Beth Zur, Gedor, Maarath, Beth Anoth, Eltekon—the Lord lists them all, knows them all. Six highland cities of Judah, each secure in His care and knowledge. Small doesn't mean unimportant to the Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Kiriath Jearim, which is Baalah—this city will later hold the ark of God. The Lord is giving Judah the very places where His glory will dwell in days to come. He settles His people, then sanctifies the land they settle.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: In the wilderness—Beth Arabah, Middin, Secacah, Nibshan, the City of Salt, and En Gedi. Even these harsh, barren places are part of Judah's inheritance. The Lord doesn't give only the pleasant places; He gives the whole land, and expects His people to be faithful everywhere.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Jebusites still hold Jerusalem—Judah couldn't drive them out. Readers today hear an echo in this verse: the inheritance promised isn't always fully possessed at once. We receive the promise, we begin to walk in it, and the full realization often waits. Yet the Lord's promise stands sure, and Jerusalem will one day be David's, then Solomon's city of God. Sometimes faith means living in the middle of the story, not at its end.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
